Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to solve a smaller piece of the same problem. Each recursive call works on a reduced input, and the process repeats until it reaches a simple case that can be solved directly—called the **base case**. By combining the results of these smaller calls, the original problem is solved without writing an explicit loop. Think of it like a set of nested Russian dolls: you keep opening a doll (making a recursive call) until you reach the tiniest one (the base case), then you close them back up in reverse order.
